content_metadata.description: An analysis of Khabib Nurmagomedov's retirement from UFC and the significance of his decision, highlighting themes of family importance and professional dedication.

qAndA.question: What was one of the injuries Khabib Nurmagomedov sustained before his fight with Justin Gaethje?
What traditional headwear did Khabib wear during his post-fight interview?

qAndA.answer: He promised his mother he would retire after this fight, likely due to the recent passing of his father and coach.
qAndA.question: What was the reason behind Khabib's decision to retire from UFC?

qAndA.answer: The Narrator lost his own father at a young age and understands the emotional weight Khabib carries.
qAndA.question: Why does the Narrator say he 'vibes with' Khabib?

qAndA.answer: Cherish your parents and prioritize your relationship with them above all else, as life is too short to take them for granted.

Apparently he was in the  hospital he broke his foot. -yeah, so... -When? Three weeks ago So he has two broken toes and a bone in his  foot that's broken or something like that, that's what his corner was telling me and uh, never told anybody, walking around so... I mean he  is one of the toughest human beings on the planet. We were elated, we were happy and then it was just  a mix of emotions then like... what's Habib doing? He just goes to the middle of the ring... is he doing  sajda? Is he prostrating? and you just see him... you just see him crouch down like a... like a little child you just see him crouch  down like a little child and... Allah hu Akbar then you realize that he's, he's crying.  He's crying because of the pressure because of   his father not being there. His father being  with him since the start of the journey and   and I guess we weren't prepared  for what he was about to say. My mother. I promise her it's gonna be my last  fight and if I give my word I have to follow this.   And him being Habib; honouring his mother's  words, announced in front of the whole world   that he is now going to quit the UFC, despite being the most dominant fighter, he's going to quit it, why? To honour the  words of his mother. And if that's not all, when he does get up and the mic's put in front  of his face, he starts advising his competitor: Gaethje, to look after his parents as well, but you  and I both know he wasn't just speaking to Gaethje   he was speaking to us all. I know a lot of  things about you. Be close with your parents because... one day it's gonna happen something  because, you never know what's gonna happen tomorrow I vibe with Habib on this because  I lost my father when I was one and a half and you only value something once you've lost  it. Many of you guys watching, whatever you're   going through you're never gonna know, you're never  gonna know, but it's best that you never know yeah,   and you have your parents because once you lose  them there's no going back after that. You know   we watch all these movies and the billion viewed songs on YouTube are to do with inappropriate relationships, but the  relationship that we are familiar with right at   the start is the son and the mother yeah, the  daughter and the mother: your mother. And Muhammad Hijab made a very good point and he said- the human  rights that we are told about nowadays it's pretty   much mostly about what you are owed and not what  you owe others yeah, there's no human rights about   the mother. But Islam makes it explicitly clear in  the primary sources like the Quran don't even say tut you know don't even make sounds like "oof" to  your mother and in the hadith we know: The mother comes first, the mother comes second,  the mother comes third and then the father comes.    So yeah after watching it I don't know I  felt like there was a lump in my throat   and I'm gonna miss that guy, you know I'm saying,  I've been you know editing videos of Habib for   since that whole Connor thing  went down and you know what each time I do it   the guy blows me away. You know some people don't  get it but, you know nowadays with how dark   the world has become, Allah sent a ray of  light. Blowing people away, on a platform with   the riches and the fame and mashaAllah doing what  he was doing. Because like famous, money, today you champion, tomorrow everything can change you know,  and you never know what's gonna happen like... most important thing for me it's family. I have no doubt  this is not the last that we've heard of Habib but I definitely am going to miss this guy. And now you're going to get the people that were   hiding underneath the rocks and the cracks and  crevasses coming out and making all these bold statements. And I know some people watching they  are not on talking terms with their parents, guys don't play games when it comes to your parents.  Even if the fault is theirs (mistake in audio) life is too short   go and apologize. You need to find ways that you  can communicate to your parents. You might need   to maybe pick up a few psychology books or go to family counselling or something.    You have to make this relationship work. May Allah  bless our brother, may Allah increase him, keep him   happy and may Allah assist the rest of us that are  going through any family problems and grant us the   ability to rectify them and become the coolness of  the eyes of our parents. And before they pass away   may Allah make it such that our parents are happy  with us. Let's leave it there guys until next time -Alhumdulilah -Asalaamu Alaikum
